🤖 **Agent note** · escalated
- **Agent:** queue worker (repo-worker-code), lane B shift
- **Session / ID:** queue task 2366 (triage)
- **Found via:** queue claim
- **Task:** Triage of #1097 — verify NIC and switch-gear facts for the core machines (epic #1080).
- **Expectation:** escalated to Drew — the switch half is documented; the NIC half needs the machines themselves.

**Triage findings (checked at current main, laptop clone origin/main):**
- Switch gear IS recorded: `doc/inventory/routing-and-switching.md` (last updated 2026-04-02) documents the core fabric — Celestica DX010 (×4, one missing fans/PSU), 32× QSFP28 **100 GbE** per switch, SONiC — plus Mellanox SX6036 and Arista 7050QX in the enrichment checklist. So the inventory's switch side exists.
- The NIC question is genuinely open: `git grep` across `doc/inventory/` and `planning/roadmaps/basement-cluster.md` finds **no NIC model, no host link-speed record for the core machines** — nothing answering "at least 200 Gb ports" one way or the other.
- One gap already visible from the docs alone: the fabric switches top out at 100 GbE per QSFP28 port, so a ≥200 Gb host attachment would require 2×100G LAG/breakout per machine — worth confirming explicitly when the NICs are read, since the LINSTOR/DRBD design in epics 4–5 depends on the real number.

**Why escalated, not routed to a code packet:** answering needs `lspci`/`ethtool` output (or a physical read) from the core machines in the basement. A queue worker has no verified hostnames/access for those machines, and guessing at hardware facts is exactly what this issue exists to prevent.

**Ask of Drew:** paste per-machine `lspci | grep -i eth` + `ethtool <iface> | grep Speed` output (or the NIC model from a physical read) on this issue — with that evidence, an agent can record it in `doc/inventory/routing-and-switching.md` and file any gap issue via a scoped follow-up packet in one pass. Blocking queue task 2366 as escalated-to-user; issue labelled `user/escalated`.
